title: Best Trampoline Parks in Asia for Kids 2026 — Updated Guide
excerpt: Trampoline parks are exploding across Asia — and they're the perfect rainy-day activity for energetic kids. We've compiled the definitive guide to the best trampoline parks from Singapore to Tokyo, Seoul to Bangkok.
content:
Trampoline parks have become the go-to activity for parents who need to burn off their kids' boundless energy in a controlled, air-conditioned environment. Asia has embraced the trend wholeheartedly, and the best trampoline parks on the continent rival anything in the United States or Europe. We visited over 25 trampoline parks across Asia with kids aged 4–14 to find the ones with the best equipment, safest environments, and most value for money.

Singapore

1. Bounce Singapore — Orchard Gateway

Best for: Ages 4+ | Location: Orchard Gateway (Somerset) | Duration: 1–2 hours | Price: SGD 18–25 per hour ($13–19 USD)

Bounce is Singapore's flagship trampoline park — a massive 20,000-square-foot facility in the heart of Orchard Road. The park features over 80 interconnected trampolines, a dodgeball court, a slam dunk zone, a 'Big Bag' landing area for practising flips (a giant airbag), and a 'Ninja Course' with obstacle challenges. The trampolines are Olympic-grade and well-maintained — the bounce is springy and consistent across the entire floor.

The park runs dedicated sessions for different age groups, including 'Rhythm & Bounce' (a music-led jumping session for all ages), 'Toddler Time' (dedicated sessions for 4–6 year olds with gentler bouncing), and 'Night Bounce' (teen sessions with music and UV lights on Friday and Saturday evenings). The on-site cafe does decent coffee and snacks, and there's a viewing gallery where parents can sit and watch.

Parent tip: Book online in advance — walk-up slots often sell out, especially on weekends. The compulsory 'Bounce socks' (SGD 3) are reusable — keep them for future visits. Toddler Time is held on weekday mornings 9–11am and is much quieter. The park is a 3-minute walk from Somerset MRT. Combine with a visit to Plaza Singapura's family-friendly attractions.

2. Jump Arena — East Coast

Best for: Ages 3+ | Location: East Coast Park | Duration: 1–1.5 hours | Price: SGD 15 per hour ($11 USD)

Jump Arena is a smaller, more affordable trampoline park located in East Coast Park. It's less flashy than Bounce but offers solid value and a more relaxed atmosphere. The park features a main trampoline area, a dodgeball court, a slam dunk zone, and a dedicated toddler area with smaller trampolines and soft play mats. The East Coast Park location means you can combine trampolining with a beach walk, cycling, or visiting the nearby Marine Cove playground.

Parent tip: Jump Arena is part of the East Coast Park complex — make a day of it with cycling, beach time, and dinner at one of the nearby restaurants. Book via the Jump Arena website for a small discount. The toddler area is excellent for 3–5 year olds.

Bangkok, Thailand

3. Bounce Thailand — The EmQuartier

Best for: Ages 5+ | Location: The EmQuartier (Phrom Phong) | Duration: 1–2 hours | Price: 450–600 THB per hour ($13–17 USD)

Bounce Thailand in Bangkok's EmQuartier mall is the sister park to Singapore's Bounce and equally impressive. The 30,000-square-foot facility features over 100 trampolines, a massive dodgeball court, a 'Wall to Wall' area where you can bounce off angled walls, a 'Foam Pit' for practising flips, and a 'Slam Dunk' zone with adjustable basketball hoops. The ninja obstacle course is among the best we've seen in Asia — a 50-metre gauntlet of balance beams, rope swings, climbing walls, and monkey bars suspended over foam pits.

The facility is impeccably clean — staff wipe down trampolines between sessions — and the safety briefing is thorough. The EmQuartier location is a bonus: the mall has a fantastic food court (Gourmet Eats on the basement level) and a beautiful outdoor garden on the 6th floor.

Kid-approved: 'I did a front flip into the foam pit! The first time I was scared but the second time I did it perfectly. The ninja course was really hard but I finished it on my third try.' — Ravi, age 9, Singapore (visiting Bangkok).

Parent tip: Bounce Thailand gets extremely busy on weekends — the queue for the dodgeball court can be 20 minutes on Saturday afternoons. Go on a weekday for a much better experience. The compulsory Bounce socks are 150 THB. The EmQuartier mall has a free shuttle from Phrom Phong BTS. Book via Klook for a 15% discount on the 90-minute session. The air conditioning can be aggressive — bring a light jacket for the viewing area.

4. Trampoline Park 365 — Rama 9

Best for: Ages 3–12 | Location: RCA (Rama 9 Road) | Duration: 1–2 hours | Price: 350–500 THB per hour ($10–14 USD)

Trampoline Park 365 is a budget-friendly alternative to Bounce Thailand. It's smaller (about 15,000 square feet) but well-maintained, with a main jumping area, a dodgeball zone, a foam pit, and a solid toddler section with mini trampolines and a ball pit. The staff are attentive and the safety standards are good. The value proposition is excellent — at 350 THB per hour, it's less than half the price of Bounce Thailand.

Parent tip: Located on RCA — best accessed by car or taxi (not near a BTS station). Weekday afternoons are the quietest. The cafe is basic — grab food at the 7-Eleven next door.

Tokyo, Japan

5. MOVED by B-Bounce — Shibuya

Best for: Ages 6+ | Location: Shibuya (near Shibuya Scramble) | Duration: 1 hour | Price: ¥2,200 per person (~$15 USD)

Japan's approach to trampoline parks is characteristically meticulous and zero-compromise. MOVED by B-Bounce in Shibuya is a premium trampoline experience — smaller than the mega-parks of Singapore and Bangkok but with a focus on quality over quantity. The trampolines are top-of-the-line European models with exceptional bounce, and the facility is spotless. The park runs structured classes ('B-Bounce Method') that teach proper jumping technique and basic tricks — surprisingly effective for kids who want to improve.

The foam pit is deep and soft, the dodgeball court uses foam balls (no bruising), and the 'Wall Bounce' area lets kids and adults bounce off walls at gravity-defying angles. The one-hour session includes a 10-minute safety briefing and 50 minutes of jumping — which is honestly enough for most kids. Japanese children are incredibly well-behaved (queueing, no pushing, taking turns) which makes the experience more pleasant for everyone.

Parent tip: Sessions must be booked online — walk-ups are not accepted. The one-hour session is timed precisely — arrive 15 minutes early for the briefing. The facility is a 7-minute walk from Shibuya Station (Hachiko exit). English-speaking staff are available but limited — the safety video has English subtitles. Combine with Shibuya Sky or a visit to the Hachiko statue.

6. Air Leap — Odaiba (Tokyo)

Best for: All ages | Location: Decks Tokyo Beach, Odaiba | Duration: 1–2 hours | Price: ¥1,800 adult / ¥1,500 child ($13 / $11 USD)

Air Leap is Japan's largest trampoline park, located in the family-friendly Odaiba entertainment district. The park features a 'Free Jump' area with 40+ interconnected trampolines, a 'Sport Zone' with dodgeball and basketball, a 'Trick Zone' with a stunt airbag, and a 'Kids Zone' for ages 3–6 with smaller trampolines and soft play elements. The Odaiba location is ideal for families — the area has dozens of attractions, restaurants, and shopping centres within walking distance.

Parent tip: Combine Air Leap with a visit to teamLab Borderless (now relocated to Odaiba), Joypolis (indoor theme park), or the Odaiba beach area. The park is a 3-minute walk from Tokyo Teleport Station. Weekday mornings are the quietest time.

Seoul, South Korea

7. Jump Seoul — Hongdae

Best for: Ages 5+ | Location: Hongdae | Duration: 1–2 hours | Price: ₩12,000–18,000 per 90 minutes (~$9–14 USD)

Seoul has embraced trampoline parks with enthusiasm, and Jump Seoul in Hongdae is one of the best. The facility is compact but well-designed, with a 'Free Jump' area, a 'Dodgeball Arena', a 'Slam Dunk' zone, and a 'Ninja Warrior' course. The Korean twist: many parks, including Jump Seoul, offer 'Jump & Dance' sessions where kids bounce to K-pop music with UV lights and glow sticks — it's a uniquely Korean experience that kids absolutely love.

The pricing is excellent — ₩12,000 for 90 minutes is roughly $9 USD, making it one of the best-value trampoline parks in Asia. The facility is clean, well-lit, and staffed by energetic young Koreans who take safety seriously but keep the vibe fun.

Parent tip: Hongdae is Seoul's youth and arts district — the area is buzzing with shops, cafes, and street performances. The park is a 5-minute walk from Hongdae Station (exit 3). Many Korean trampoline parks require participants to watch a mandatory safety video — allow an extra 10 minutes before your session. Bring a Korean phrasebook or use Papago — English staff availability varies.

Hong Kong

8. Ryze Hong Kong — Quarry Bay

Best for: Ages 6+ | Location: Quarry Bay (Taikoo Place) | Duration: 1–2 hours | Price: HKD 130–160 per 45 minutes ($17–20 USD)

Ryze is Hong Kong's premier trampoline park, featuring over 50 interconnected trampolines covering the entire floor — a layout that lets jumpers bounce continuously around the entire park without touching solid ground. The park has a dodgeball court, a slam dunk zone, a foam pit, and a dedicated 'Fit' zone for high-intensity interval training on trampolines (surprisingly popular with Hong Kong fitness enthusiasts).

The Quarry Bay location is convenient — it's a 2-minute walk from Taikoo Place, a major office and retail complex. The park runs 'Mini Jump' sessions for 3–5 year olds on weekday mornings (HKD 110 for 45 minutes) — the only trampoline park in Hong Kong with dedicated toddler sessions.

Parent verdict: 'Ryze was a lifesaver during our Hong Kong trip. Our 7-year-old had been cooped up in the hotel because of rain, and one hour at Ryze turned her from a grumpy gremlin into a happy bouncing machine. The interconnected trampoline layout is genius — she just bounced around in circles for an hour.' — Sarah, mother of one, Australia.

Parent tip: Ryze Hong Kong sells out on weekends — book online at least 3 days in advance. The 45-minute session is the standard option and feels about right for most kids (the 90-minute session leads to tired, wobbly legs). The compulsory Ryze socks are HKD 20. The Taikoo Place complex has dozens of dining options (including a food court on the ground floor). Combine with a visit to the nearby Quarry Bay Promenade or the Hong Kong Film Archive.

Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia

9. Jump Street Asia — Bangsar

Best for: Ages 4+ | Location: Bangsar Shopping Centre | Duration: 1–2 hours | Price: RM 25–35 per hour ($6–8 USD)

Jump Street Asia in KL's Bangsar district offers exceptional value — RM 25 per hour (about $6 USD) makes it one of the cheapest trampoline parks in the region. The quality doesn't suffer, though: the park has a spacious free-jump area with well-maintained trampolines, a dodgeball zone, a foam pit, and a toddler zone. The staff are attentive and the facility is clean. For Malaysian families, the value proposition is unbeatable — a family of four can jump for an hour for under RM 100.

Parent tip: Located in Bangsar Shopping Centre — one of KL's most family-friendly malls. The park is busiest on weekends. There's a dedicated parent viewing area with free WiFi. The Bangsar LRT station is a 10-minute walk away.

Quick Comparison

  • Best overall: Bounce Thailand (EmQuartier, Bangkok) — largest, best equipment, great mall setting
  • Best value: Jump Street Asia (KL) — RM 25/hour, excellent quality for the price
  • Best for toddlers: Ryze Hong Kong (Mini Jump sessions for 3–5 year olds)
  • Best for teens: MOVED by B-Bounce (Tokyo) — structured trick-learning classes
  • Best unique experience: Jump Seoul (Hongdae) — K-pop jump and dance sessions with UV lights
  • Best for a rainy day: Bounce Singapore (Orchard) — central location, covered by Orchard Road shopping
  • Best ninja course: Bounce Thailand (EmQuartier) — 50-metre obstacle gauntlet

Practical Tips

  • Book online: Almost every trampoline park on this list offers online booking with a small discount. Walk-ups are frequently turned away at peak times.
  • Bring or buy special socks: Nearly every park requires grip socks (non-slip socks with rubber grips on the bottom). Some parks include them in the ticket, most sell them for $2–4.
  • Hydrate: Jumping on a trampoline is surprisingly intense cardio. Kids will be sweating within minutes. Most parks have water fountains — some don't. Bring a water bottle.
  • Know the rules: Basic safety: one jumper per trampoline, no double-bouncing, land on both feet, no flips without foam pit or supervision. Parks enforce these strictly — violations can mean early termination of your session.
  • Consider timing: Trampoline parks are noticeably quieter 9am–12pm on weekdays. Weekend afternoons are peak chaos. Late evening sessions (7–10pm) attract older crowds and teens.

Our verdict: Trampoline parks are the ultimate high-energy indoor activity for kids across Asia. Bounce Thailand and Bounce Singapore are the flagship experiences — large, well-run, and consistently excellent. For budget-conscious families, Jump Street Asia in KL and Jump Seoul offer incredible value. And for a uniquely Japanese experience, MOVED by B-Bounce in Shibuya is worth every yen. Whatever your city and whatever the weather, there's a trampoline park ready to wear out your kids — in the best possible way.
author: Kids Activities Asia Team
